Prospective blind discovery: across all 5 XGBoost evaluation scripts (e.g., MultivariableXGBoost_testing_best_unique_35f.py), main() directly invokes (1) calculate_calibration() (L37-57, L173), binarizing predicted survival times into hard {0,1} y_pred_binary passed to linregress() and 10-bin CalibrationDisplay.from_predictions(); (2) calculate_concordance_index() (L65-85, L176), dropping all event-free survivors beyond horizon (mask = y_true < days) and calling concordance_index(y_true_period, y_pred_period) without event_observed; and (3) overall concordance_index(y_true, y_pred) at L158 also omitting event_observed (despite passing event_observed=(y_upper == y_lower) to kmf.fit() at L165). Although the published article noted that the AFT XGBoost comparator did not allow individual probability calculations and could therefore not be calibrated in primary plots, all five official evaluation scripts still executed the binarized calibration routine directly inside main() alongside the uncensored and survivor-dropping C-index calculations.
